deep.reconstruction:
The page is one sheet of a long, continuous numerical table running across ff. 195-197 and beyond. There is no derivation on it. It has four blocks of 50 rows each: x = 7.150-7.250, 7.250-7.350, 7.350-7.450 and 7.450, the last row of one block repeated as the first row of the next.

Each block has four columns:
(i) the argument x, in equal steps h = 0.002;
(ii) an angle f(x), in degrees, minutes and seconds, with seconds to 5 decimals. It runs from 154°46'45.84366" at x = 7.150 to 160°11'19.37826" at x = 7.450;
(iii) the first difference D1(x) = f(x+h) - f(x), in seconds of arc. Example: 154°49'13.48857" - 154°46'45.84366" = 2'27.64491" = 147.64491";
(iv) the second difference D2 = D1(x-h) - D1(x), in units of 10^-5 arcsecond. Example: 147.64491 - 147.37952 = 0.26539, written 26539.

The first differences fall from about 147.6" to 113.8" across the page, i.e. df/dx falls from about 0.358 to 0.275 rad per unit. The second differences fall smoothly from 26597 to 19391, and the third differences are nearly constant at about -0.00055" to -0.0004". This is the standard technique of building a table by differences, or checking a computed table by differencing. A smooth third-difference sequence certifies the values to about 10^-5".

The rows x = 7.156 and 7.256 carry a horizontal stroke. My conjecture: these mark control points computed directly, every 0.1.

What function is being tabulated is not stated on this page or the adjacent ones. My diagnostics:
- f increases toward roughly 180° with decreasing slope.
- cot(f/2) takes the values 0.28970, 0.22372, 0.17463 at x = 6.85, 7.15, 7.45. These fit roughly A + B·e^{-0.99x} with A ≈ 0.035.
- dfdx/(π - f) ≈ 0.84, 0.81, 0.80.
- The fit is not an exact pendulum separatrix (4·arctan(e^x) - π), a pure exponential approach, or a simple energy law f'^2 = A + B·cos^2(f/2).

So the function stays unidentified. It is plausibly an anomaly-type angle (e.g. from orbital or rotational motion) as a function of time or a logarithmic variable, perhaps connected with problems in Lagrange's Mécanique analytique (2nd ed., vol. 2, 1815/16), given the bundle name. That last point is speculation.
errors: Spot checks of first differences (rows 7.150-7.160, 7.174, 7.196-7.212, 7.316-7.320, 7.348, 7.438, 7.448) are all arithmetically exact.
Spot-checked second differences are exact (e.g. 25958 at 7.172, 25168 at 7.200, 24211 at 7.236, 23100 at 7.280).

The third differences around x = 7.198-7.202 run 25284, 25231, 25168, 25122 (steps -53, -63, -46). This hints that f(7.200) may be off by about 3×10^-5 arcsec. That is at the noise level of the last digit and is not a real error.

results.what: High-precision table (to 1e-5 arcsec) of an unidentified smooth angle function f(x), x = 7.150..7.450 in steps of 0.002, with first and second differences as a control.
results.modern_name: Construction and checking of a function table by finite differences
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 17th-19th century practice (Briggs, Newton, Mouton; later Prony's tables)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine computational table with difference checks; Gauss is well known for producing many such tables. The only open point is which function is tabulated, which this page does not reveal.
